title: A mind that rests on nothing (section 10)
word: A mind that rests on nothing
hookLine: a mind should arise that rests on nothing: the line said to have woken Huineng

cards: A young man is selling firewood in a market town in southern China. He's poor, and the old account says he can't read. He delivers a load to a shop, and on the way out he hears a man reciting something.
The words stop him where he stands. What is that? The Diamond Sutra, comes the answer.
That's how the Platform Sutra, the book of this young man's life and teaching, tells it. His name is Huineng, and Chan and Zen remember him as a great ancestor.
Later in the same account, one line of that sutra opens him all the way. It's today's.

teach.b: First, a look back. The Buddha asks Subhuti: long ago, with the Buddha Dipankara, did the Tathagata receive any teaching? No, Subhuti says.
Nothing was received. Second, adorning. Does a bodhisattva adorn the Buddha-lands, make the worlds beautiful?
No, because adorning is not adorning; that's why it's called adorning. It's the rhythm of the earlier sections. Third, the line.
Therefore, the Buddha says, a bodhisattva should give rise to a pure mind like this: a mind that doesn't rest on sights, sounds, smells, tastes, touches or thoughts.

teach.h: A MIND THAT RESTS ON NOTHING.
teach.b: A mind should arise that rests on nothing. Notice it doesn't say no mind should arise. The mind sees, hears, works.

It just doesn't set up camp. A hand that catches a ball and lets it go is still a hand. Tradition says that later, when Huineng's teacher explained the sutra to him, it was at this line that he woke up completely.
Giving without resting on anything. Not seen by marks. Even the raft.
Nothing fixed. Four lines. No I have attained.
Each was a place where the mind could have settled and made a home: the gift, the statue, the teaching, the prize, the credit. Each time, the sutra let it lift off again.
Today's line names what was happening all week: the same mind, just not resting.

how: In Chan and Zen this line is studied closely and often recited, and the story of Huineng hearing the Diamond Sutra is told in the Platform Sutra, a text read in those schools.

games.q: what does “a mind that rests on nothing” mean?
o: a mind that works but doesn't settle or cling anywhere
a mind that refuses to see, hear or think at all
a mind emptied of every thought, sight and sound

p: a mind that rests on nothing
the line said to have woken Huineng
a firewood seller who heard the sutra

s: the line says no mind should arise at all
a mind should arise; it just shouldn't rest on sights, sounds or thoughts.

he's delivering firewood and hears a man reciting it.

adorning is not adorning, Subhuti says; that's why it's called adorning.

games.q: you're Huineng, selling firewood. a line from a stranger's recitation stops you in your tracks. what do you do?
o: finish the delivery and forget it.
ask what the text is, and where it's taught.
wait for him to recite it again tomorrow.
games.why: he asks. the Platform Sutra says he learns it's the Diamond Sutra and hears of a teacher who teaches it, and he sets out to find him.

practice: Let sounds come, a car, a fridge, your own breathing, and notice the mind land on one: that's a truck, that's too loud. Then let it lift, the way a bird lifts off a wire.
You don't have to stop the landing; just catch one moment of lifting, and stay in the open space after it as long as it lasts.

wordCard.voice: A mind that rests on nothing. A mind that arises without resting on sights, sounds or thoughts: the line tradition says woke Huineng. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: not resting, not set down; the sutra's word for a mind that settles on nothing.

carryVoice: Your line: resting on nothing. A bird on a wire, then open sky. That's the week, gathered up.
